# New-ZbxTemplate

## SYNOPSIS

Creates a template.

## SYNTAX

```
New-ZbxTemplate [[-Name] <string>] [-Uuid <string>] [-DisplayName <string>] [-Description <string>] [-VendorName <string>] [-VendorVersion <string>] [-Group <ZabbixReference<ZabbixTemplateGroup>[]>] [-LinkedTemplate <ZabbixReference<ZabbixTemplate>[]>] [-Tag <ZabbixTagRequest[]>] [-Macro <ZabbixTemplateMacroRequest[]>] [-WizardReady <ZabbixTemplateWizardReady>] [-Readme <string>] [-AdditionalProperty <Hashtable>] [-Force] [-InputObject <PSObject>] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

A template is a reusable set of items, triggers, graphs, discovery rules and dashboards; linking it to a host gives the host all of them. The New-ZbxTemplate cmdlet sends template.create with one request field per parameter, then reads the new template back with template.get and writes it. The server requires -Name and -Group; -AdditionalProperty sets any other field by its API name and wins over a parameter. -WhatIf shows what would be created, and the command needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Create a template in a template group

```powershell
New-ZbxTemplate -Host 'Nginx by HTTP' -Group 'Templates/Web' | Select-Object TemplateId, HostName
```

-Host is the template's technical name; -Group takes template group names, ids or objects. The created template is read back and written.

### Example 2: Create a template that links another, with tags and a macro

```powershell
New-ZbxTemplate -Host 'Web App Nginx' -Group 'Templates/Web' -LinkedTemplate 'Nginx by HTTP' `
    -Description 'Nginx in front of the shop' -Tag @{ tag = 'class'; value = 'software' } `
    -Macro @{ macro = '{$NGINX.PORT}'; value = '8080' } | Out-Null
Get-ZbxTemplate -Name 'Web App Nginx' -SelectParentTemplates -SelectTags -SelectMacros |
    Select-Object HostName, Description,
        @{ n = 'Links'; e = { $_.ParentTemplates.HostName } },
        @{ n = 'Macros'; e = { $_.Macros.Macro } }
```

-LinkedTemplate nests templates: 'Web App Nginx' brings along everything 'Nginx by HTTP' has. -Tag and -Macro take hashtables shaped like the API's objects.

### Example 3: Create a template, give it an item and link it to a host

```powershell
$template = New-ZbxTemplate -Host 'Nginx by HTTP' -Group 'Templates/Web'
$template | New-ZbxItem -Name 'Nginx status' -Key 'nginx.status' -Type Trapper -ValueType Text | Out-Null
Set-ZbxHost 'web-01' -Template $template | Out-Null
Get-ZbxItem -Host 'web-01' -Name 'Nginx*' | Select-Object HostId, Name, Key
```

The written template can be piped on: New-ZbxItem binds -HostId from its TemplateId.

Represents a reference to an API object: a parameter that points at an API object takes its id, its name, or the object itself piped from a Get- cmdlet, and becomes an id before the call — one parameter, three spellings, one resolution.
